rationale: Interpret the completed receipt for the registered question and extend the account with an isolating successor experiment. The sampled operands confirm the source prediction: re-synchronizing a replica that already accepted the StopSign inflates its reported accepted index by one (accepted 7 over six indices of content on the two followers, events 22 and 23), its read of the StopSign's own index 5 returns None, its decided-log read from 0 collapses to the StopSign alone, and a write quorum of inflated reports let the leader decide index 7 while holding six indices, which flipped the leader's own reconfiguration endpoint from true to false and made its decided log unreadable (event 24). The no-reconnect control stayed consistent (events 9-11), so the change is attributable to the re-established-connection path. The interpretation is therefore moved to violated/asserted, the behavior about the index accounting is re-conditioned on the execution, a second behavior records the resulting index shift and decided-log read loss, the registered gap is answered with the traced producer path, and a successor experiment is submitted that re-synchronizes only one follower to separate the follower-local effect from the leader's phantom decision.

investigations.discriminator: Whether a single re-synchronized replica already flips its own StopSign-decided endpoint and decided-log read without the leader forming a decision on a quorum of inflated reports (targeted by the successor experiment's single case), and whether the snapshot-enabled branch of create_log_sync inflates the same way.

knowledge.statement: InternalStorage::sync_log sets accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and, when LogSync.stopsign is Some, adds one further index for that StopSign before returning; it does not subtract the LogSync's prefix, so when sync_idx already addresses the StopSign's own index the replica's accepted index ends up one larger than the entries it holds. SequencePaxos::create_log_sync does not adjust sync_idx for a StopSign already present on the sender: it uses common_prefix_idx unchanged and attaches the sender's stored StopSign.
knowledge.conditions: Reached when a follower applies an AcceptSync whose LogSync carries stopsign = Some; the accounting is unconditional with respect to whether the resumed prefix already contained a StopSign. Exercised in receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8: both re-synchronized followers ended with accepted index 7 over a log of five entries plus a StopSign (events 22, 23), while all four sampled states before the re-synchronization were 6/6 (events 19, 20, 21) and the no-reconnect control stayed at 6/6 (events 9, 10, 11).

knowledge.statement: On a replica that already holds the accepted StopSign, applying an AcceptSync whose LogSync carries that StopSign leaves the stored log unchanged while the reported accepted index rises by one; the replica's read of the StopSign's previous index (5) then returns None, its read of the next index (6) returns the StopSign, and read_decided_suffix(0) returns a decided log of one element (the StopSign) rather than the six elements it returned before, because the internal index-type decision places the StopSign at accepted_idx - 1.
knowledge.conditions: Three-node cluster, five decided entries plus a StopSign, no snapshots (NoSnapshot), default batch size, re-synchronization triggered by a follower's public reconnected() call after the StopSign was accepted and decided; observed on node 1 and node 2 in receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 (events 22, 23) against their own pre-resynchronization state (events 19, 20) and the no-reconnect control (events 10, 11).

knowledge.assertion: sync_log adds the StopSign carried by LogSync on top of sync_idx + suffix.len()

interpretations.rationale: Confirmed by execution: the re-synchronization of a replica that already accepted its configuration's StopSign inflates its reported accepted index by one, and a write quorum of such reports makes the leader decide an index past every entry it holds. Receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8, two cases in one run over three real OmniPaxos instances with MemoryStorage (events: 19,20,21 = after the StopSign was decided on all three nodes; 22,23 = the two re-synchronized followers; 24 = the leader; 9,10,11 = the identical prefix without reconnected()). Before the re-synchronization all three nodes reported accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, read(5) = StopSign with decided = true, and read_decided_suffix(0) = six elements. After both followers called reconnected(3): node 1 and node 2 reported accepted 7 over the same six indices of content, their read(5) returned None (the StopSign is now placed at index 6 by the internal index-type rule), and their decided-log read from 0 returned a single element (the StopSign), so the five decided entries disappeared from the readable decided log while is_reconfigured stayed true; node 3 (leader) reported decided 7 with accepted 6, is_reconfigured false where it had been true, read(5) = StopSign with decided = false, and read_decided_suffix(0) = None, i.e. the user on the leader can no longer read the decided log at all and never observes the reconfiguration as complete. The declared comparisons match this reading: comparison 2 (leader reports the reconfiguration as decided) violated at index 24, comparison 3 (decided index covered by entries held) violated at index 24, comparison 4 (leader's decided log readable from 0) violated at index 24, comparison 5 (re-synchronized follower's decided log still has the five entries plus the StopSign) violated at indices 22 and 23, while comparisons 0 and 1 (the same predicates before the reconnection, indices 19-21) and comparisons 6 and 7 (the no-reconnect control, indices 9-11) hold, which attributes the change to the re-synchronization rather than to the reconfiguration or to the sampling.

27bf7fc0875c4342966bd3dc15df80ec-gap-0.explanation: The legitimate producer path was observed end to end: node 1 and node 2 each called the public reconnected(3) after the StopSign had been accepted and decided; reconnected() sets the follower to Phase::Recover and sends PrepareReq with its current promise (agent-source/omnipaxos/src/sequence_paxos/mod.rs 343-357); the leader in Phase::Accept handles it via handle_preparereq, resets the follower's promise state and re-sends Prepare (leader.rs 66-74); the follower, now in Phase::Recover with its promise equal to the Prepare's ballot, re-promises with accepted_idx = 6, an index that already counts its stored StopSign (follower.rs 13-51, internal_storage.rs 503-512); handle_promise_accept then calls send_accsync (leader.rs 301-314), and because the promise's accepted round equals the leader's current ballot, send_accsync takes its first branch and uses the follower's own accepted index as the valid prefix (leader.rs 150-191), producing LogSync{sync_idx: 6, suffix: [], stopsign: Some} from create_log_sync (mod.rs 405-432); sync_log then adds the StopSign once more (internal_storage.rs 313-360). Receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 confirms the outcome on the sampled endpoints (events 22 and 23).

counterevidence: The no-reconnect control case of the same execution kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read at indices 9-11), so the deviation is attributable to the re-established-connection path and not to the reconfiguration, to the harness, or to reading the log.

The documented user flow for reconfiguration (agent-source/docs/omnipaxos/reconfiguration.md 25-34) expects the user to start a new instance once a node observes LogEntry::StopSign(ss, true); a user who stops the old instance immediately limits the user-facing window, but does not remove the defect: the leader of the same run never observes the StopSign as decided after the corruption (is_reconfigured false, decided log unreadable), and the two followers keep reporting the reconfiguration as decided while their decided log silently loses the five decided entries.

The leader's phantom decision is inferred from its own reported state (decided 7 with accepted 6 and six indices of content) plus the two followers' inflated 7; the internal accepted-index vector was not sampled, so the assignment of which reports formed the quorum rests on the source rule (handle_accepted decides any incoming accepted index reaching a write quorum) rather than on a direct trace of that vector.
limitations: No snapshots (NoSnapshot entries) and default batch size 1: whether the snapshot-enabled branch of create_log_sync inflates the same way is untested.

Messages were delivered in FIFO order without loss and without tick()-driven timers, so the re-established-connection call is the only recovery trigger exercised; loss-triggered re-synchronization is untested.

All three nodes used in-memory storage; persistence across a restart and the behaviour of other storages on out-of-range reads (a storage-implementer responsibility per the Storage trait) were not exercised.

The re-synchronization needed two followers of a three-node cluster to inflate for the leader to decide the phantom index 7; the single-replica case is targeted by the successor experiment submitted with this update.

a re-synchronized replica's decided log read shrinks to the StopSign alone

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a third case that re-synchronizes only one follower to separate the follower-local index inflation from the leader's phantom decision, and adds a read of index 6 plus its baseline to show where the index accounting places the StopSign.

scope.description: Three cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network: (resync) both followers report re-established connections, (single) only node 1 does, (control) neither does. Public API only; each lifecycle stage emits its own CA_EVENT name.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot, so T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() is false and create_log_sync takes its no-snapshot branch.
ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } (majority 2) and default ServerConfig (batch_size 1).
Leadership is established with try_become_leader() on node 3; BLE messages are dropped because no tick() is called.
All SequencePaxos messages are delivered in FIFO order without loss.
excluded: Snapshots, trimming, compaction and batching are not exercised.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

experiment.prefix: Same prefix as the fixed 27bf7fc0875c4342966bd3dc15df80ec-experiment: node 3 leads (try_become_leader), five entries are appended and decided, a StopSign is proposed with reconfigure() and decided; SAMPLE lines (now also carrying read_idx6) are emitted per lifecycle stage. Case resync calls node1.reconnected(3) and node2.reconnected(3); case single calls only node1.reconnected(3); case control calls neither; every case then drains the FIFO queue to quiet and samples nodes 1, 2 and 3.

comparisons.description: Reproduction in the successor run: after both followers report re-established connections the leader still reports the reconfiguration as decided.
Reproduction: a re-synchronized follower's decided log read from index 0 still contains the five decided entries plus the StopSign.
Baseline before any re-synchronization: index 6 holds no StopSign.
A single re-synchronized follower still reports the reconfiguration as decided.
A single re-synchronized follower's reported decided index stays covered by the entries it holds.
A single re-synchronized follower still reports the StopSign at its own index 5.
A single re-synchronized follower still has a six-element decided log read from index 0.
With only one inflated report the leader still reports the reconfiguration as decided.
With only one inflated report the leader's decided index stays covered by the entries it holds.

semantic_changes: New case single (only node 1 reconnects) plus a read of index 6 in every sample; the resync and control cases are retained unchanged apart from the added read_idx6 field.
Compared fields are read from the same public endpoints as before; no production code was modified.
